title: Simulation-driven Compliance Evidence Framework
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Summary:
This playbook defines a repeatable, measurable framework for producing and validating compliance evidence using controlled simulations. The goal is to reduce audit risk by exercising RBAC, audit logging, data residency controls, secure SDLC gates, and incident response paths in realistic, automated ways that surface evidence gaps before an external audit or real incident.

Why simulations?
- Produces concrete artifacts (logs, alerts, change approvals) on a schedule rather than waiting for chance occurrences.
- Validates the end-to-end evidence chain (who, what, why, when) across systems.
- Exercises people, automation, and tooling in low-risk environments.

Scope and assumptions:
- Scope: Accounts, service principals, feature flags, deployment pipelines (CI), audit-log ingestion, retention manifests, and incident tooling (pager, ticketing, forensics).
- Not in scope: production data corruption, customer-visible outages. Simulations must be safe and reversible.

Objectives:
1. Demonstrate RBAC change traceability for at least 3 role families (admin, infra, deployment) per quarter.
2. Verify retention and residency metadata are attached to simulated inference logs and archived according to policy.
3. Validate secure-SDLC gate evidence (code review, dependency scan, signing) for a canary model rollout.
4. Exercise incident response evidence capture (forensic logs, snapshots, chain-of-custody) and prove packaging within SLA.

Roles and ownership:
- Security (owner): design simulations, review outputs, approve evidence packages.
- Eng-SRE: provide isolated simulation namespaces and retention buckets.
- Eng-Serving-Runtime: produce model-serving telemetry simulation harness.
- Compliance: accept packaged artifacts as readiness indicator for audits.
- Product (optional): sign off simulations that touch customer-facing flows.

Simulation types and cadence:
- Authz mutation simulations (monthly): create, modify, revoke test entitlements to validate entitlement-provenance pipelines.
- Audit-log replay and enrichment (weekly): inject synthetic inference events with residency tags and verify ingestion and queryability.
- Pipeline-gate smoke (bi-weekly): push a guarded canary through CI with synthetic code-sign artifacts to validate SDLC gates.
- Incident tabletop with live evidence capture (quarterly): trigger a controlled simulated incident that causes alerting and automated forensic capture.

Preconditions and safety checks:
1. All simulations run against pre-provisioned test tenants and never include customer PII.
2. Feature-flag controls with immediate rollback.
3. Automated blast-radius guardrails: quota caps, time-limited credentials, and network egress restrictions.
4. Approval checklist: simulation owner, SRE approver, security approver.

Procedure: Authz Mutation Simulation (example)
1. Create a named test principal: sim-authz-2026-q2 and attach one of the target roles.
2. Perform a scripted set of actions that exercise permissions that role grants (API calls, deployment triggers).
3. Revoke the role and rotate the principal credentials.
4. Validate recorded artifacts: change request ID, signed approval, role-binding event in IAM audit, API call traces in service logs, correlated alert in SIEM.
5. Package evidence and submit to compliance.

Command examples and snippets:
- Create a test service account (CLI):
  redwood iam service-account create --name sim-authz-2026-q2 --project sim-tenant
- Example playback of a synthetic inference log event (JSON):
  {
    "event_type": "inference.request",
    "tenant_id": "sim-tenant",
    "model": "gpt-sim-1",
    "residency": "eu",
    "retention_policy": "30d",
    "timestamp": "2026-03-15T12:01:22Z"
  }
- SIEM query sample (ELK):
  index=audit-* AND tenant_id:sim-tenant AND event_type:inference.request | sort @timestamp desc | limit 50

Acceptance criteria and metrics:
- Every simulation run must produce a minimum evidence bundle with the following items: change-request ID, signed approval, raw audit logs, parsed index entry, retention metadata manifest, and a packaging manifest.
- Targets: 95% of simulation runs must meet packaging completeness; median evidence-generation time must be < 2 hours from simulation start.
- False-positives: simulations must not generate pager alerts to production on-call. Any such occurrence triggers a blameless postmortem.

Artifacts and evidence packaging (table)
- artifact_type | required_format | retention_location | responsible_team | verification_step
- change_request | PDF/HTML | compliance-bucket/simulations/{date} | security | checksum + signer
- approvals | signed-email/SCIM | compliance-bucket/simulations/{date} | people-ops/security | cross-ref to ticket
- raw_audit_logs | ndjson | immutable-audit-store/simulations/{date} | eng-sre | schema-validate + hash
- indexed_entries | jsonl | search-cluster/index-audit-sim | eng-platform | queryable via sample query
- forensic_snapshot | tar.gz (encrypted) | forensic-vault/{date} | eng-serving-runtime | GPG signature and chain-of-custody note

Packaging checklist (required):
1. Verify all artifact hashes match recorded manifest.
2. Confirm residency and retention metadata present on each artifact.
3. Confirm that the evidence package has a sealed signature (KMS-wrapped) and a recorded owner.
4. Upload package to compliance bucket and emit notification to compliance@redwood.com with package ID.

Escalation and exceptions:
- If a simulation cannot produce a required artifact due to tooling failure, record the failure, open a ticket to eng-sre with priority P1 if it affects > 2 simulations, and mark the run as failed.
- Exception process: temporary deviation allowed only with security and compliance written approval and an entry in the Risk Exceptions register with mitigation and TTL.

Measuring readiness and continuous improvement:
- Quarterly simulation retrospectives run by security and SRE to identify flaky tooling, gaps in evidence chain, and process improvements.
- Maintain a simulation health dashboard with run success rate, artifact completeness, median packaging time, and accidental pager incidents.

Appendix: Example packaging manifest (JSON-Lines, one-per-line)
{"package_id":"sim-2026q2-0007","run_id":"sim-2026q2-0007-run1","artifacts":["change_request.pdf","raw_audit.ndjson","index.jsonl","forensic.tgz"],"owner":"Aisha Patel","start_ts":"2026-03-15T12:00:00Z","end_ts":"2026-03-15T13:20:00Z"}

Note: the manifest above is illustrative; the real manifest file is NDJSON with top-level fields flattened for archival.
